title: Equality of Opportunity in Supervised Learning
authors: Moritz Hardt, Eric Price, Nathan Srebro
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS/NeurIPS 2016), vol. 29, pp. 3323-3331
conclusions: Proposes 'equalized odds' and the weaker 'equal opportunity' as oblivious non-discrimination criteria for a predictor with respect to a protected attribute A and true outcome Y, contrasted with demographic parity.

Gives a constructive, post-processing method: given any existing (possibly discriminatory) predictor or score, derive a new predictor using only the joint distribution of (Y, A, predictor/score) via group-specific (possibly randomized) thresholds, without retraining or touching features X.

Formulates the optimal derived predictor as a small linear program over per-group true/false-positive rates and shows the equalized-odds predictor corresponds to the pointwise-minimum ROC curve across groups.

Proves a Bayes-optimality/near-optimality result: an optimal equalized-odds or equal-opportunity predictor can be derived from the Bayes-optimal regressor and A, with a bound relating suboptimal regressors to loss via a Kolmogorov-distance argument.

Demonstrates the approach on real FICO credit-score data across four race groups, comparing max-profit, race-blind, demographic-parity, equal-opportunity, and equalized-odds thresholds and their profit trade-offs (99.3% / 92.8% / 69.8% of max profit respectively for race-blind, equal opportunity, demographic parity).
Frames its own method explicitly as a post-processing / post-hoc step applied to an already-trained predictor, not a training-time constraint.
our_use: main.tex:198-200, in the 'Resource-constrained classification' related-work paragraph: 'In fair classification, post-processing likewise edits a trained model's decisions with group-specific thresholds \citep{hardt2016equality}.'
